business_scope.primary_industry_name: Vacuum Freeze-Drying Manufacture of Organic Pet Treats and Meal Kibble

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (English common law tradition under a bijural federal framework; Quebec civil law not applicable to BC)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA/USMCA), in force 1 July 2020
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the EU (provisional application since 21 September 2017)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), in force for Canada 30 December 2018
Convention Between Canada and the United States of America for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1980, as amended by Protocol of 21 September 2007)
Agreement between the Government of Canada and the Government of the People's Republic of China for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (FIPA), in force 1 October 2014

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, SBC 2002, c. 57 (ss. 1, 22-24, 51.1-51.4, 196-198); Business Corporations Regulation, B.C. Reg. 265/2022; unlimited liability company designation and name requirements under s. 51.2.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registry Services, Corporate Registry Division, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia; online filing exclusively through BC Corporate Online / OneStop Business Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form 1), Notice of Articles (Form 2), Articles of Incorporation, and Consent to Act as Director (Form 4); Certificate of Incorporation issued under s. 197 of the Business Corporations Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow account requirement in British Columbia; the ULC may be formed with nominal authorized capital and shares subscribed at par value or issued without par value post-filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the incorporation of the Company under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia) is approved, and the Incorporation Application, Notice of Articles, and Articles as submitted are ratified. RESOLVED FURTHER: The authorized share capital is subscribed by the founding shareholders per Schedule 'A', consideration is satisfied as stated, and share certificates are issued. RESOLVED FURTHER: The registered office and records office are established at the Notice of Articles address, and banking mandate and records custody are approved. RESOLVED FURTHER: [Name], [Name], and [Name] are appointed Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, with authority to execute ancillary documents. RESOLVED FURTHER: Management secures all CFIA, municipal, environmental, and industrial permits to commence freeze-dried raw pet meat manufacturing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services — BC Corporate Online / OneStop Business Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search report through a BC Registry-authorized provider; verify uniqueness and compliance with s. 22-24 of the Business Corporations Act; reserve the corporate name for 56 days; the name must include 'ULC', 'Unlimited Liability Company', or the approved French equivalent to signal unlimited shareholder liability.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report (issued within 56 days)
Authorized agent authorization letter (if filing by agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a revised NUANS request or a departmental name reconsideration; provide consents or distinguishing features from conflicting name holders within the 56-day reservation period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Incorporation Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate legal counsel, notary public, and incorporators holding BCeID credentials
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the ULC Articles including unlimited liability designation, authorized share structure, class rights, and restrictions; complete Form 1 (Incorporation Application), Form 2 (Notice of Articles), and Form 4 (Consent to Act as Director); each incorporator executes the Incorporation Application before a witness or notary as applicable.
required_dossiers: Form 4 — Consent to Act as Director for each named director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to registrar requisitions by amending and re-executing the Articles or forms; the registrar may issue a correction notice under s. 268 of the Business Corporations Act for minor defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registrar of Companies — BC Corporate Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed incorporation package via BC Corporate Online; pay the combined incorporation and first annual report fee (CAD 354.75, approximately USD 260); the system issues an electronic Certificate of Incorporation under s. 197, which constitutes the statutory date of the company's existence.
required_dossiers: Completed incorporation package (Form 1, Form 2, Articles, Form 4)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing is queried, correct and resubmit within the registrar's requisition period; if the application is deemed abandoned, refile with fresh signatures and execution dates.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Organizational Meeting, Officer Appointment, and Registered Office Ratification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the ULC; corporate secretary; registered records office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting, waiving notice, and approve the organizational agenda: ratify incorporation; authorize share issuance and the share ledger; appoint officers; adopt the corporate seal; confirm the registered office and records office address; approve the corporate bank mandate and signing authorities.
required_dossiers: Written minutes of the first board meeting
Form 3 — Notice of Change of Registered Office (if address differs from the Notice of Articles)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure any procedural omission by written unanimous board consent; re-file Form 3 if the records address is corrected or challenged by the registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Registrations and Licensing Intake
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), BC Ministry of Finance, municipal licensing office, and Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the ULC with CRA for a Business Number (corporate income tax, GST/HST, payroll, and import/export accounts); if US-resident shareholders hold the ULC, file IRS Form 8832 check-the-box election for pass-through treatment; apply for the municipal business licence and initiate the CFIA Safe Food for Canadians Act pet food processor licence application; file the initial annual report (Form 11) with BC Registry within two months after each incorporation anniversary.
required_dossiers: Notice of Articles and list of directors/officers
CRA RC1A Business Number registration or online CRA program registration
CFIA Safe Food for Canadians Act licence application (pet food processing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resubmit corrected registrations to CRA or the provincial registrar upon rejection; appeal a municipal licence refusal to the municipal licensing board; provide supplementary food safety declarations to CFIA within the response window.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA), Western Region Licensing and Registration Division, coordinated with the BC Ministry of Agriculture and Food and the municipal industrial business licensing authority where the freeze-drying facility is located.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Safe Food for Canadians Act (S.C. 2012, c. 24) Licence for Pet Food Processing, together with the Municipal Industrial Business Licence for Freeze-Dried Pet Food Manufacturing.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy (ENV) — Environmental Protection Division
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B — Registration and sectoral authorization under the Environmental Management Act (EMA); a full Environmental Assessment Certificate is not triggered for a small-scale freeze-drying facility below the Reviewable Projects Regulation (B.C. Reg. 370/2002) production thresholds; operations are governed by a low-impact EMA registration and municipal wastewater discharge approval.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: Municipal Sewage Regulation (B.C. Reg. 100/2012) — BOD5, total suspended solids, and oil/grease limits, with a discharge permit required if non-municipal effluent exceeds thresholds; Air: compliance with BC Air Quality Objectives and EMA Part 3 for PM2.5, PM10, ammonia, and VOCs from freeze-drying systems; Waste: Waste Discharge Regulation (B.C. Reg. 298/99) for offal and organic solids, and the federal Ozone-depleting Substances Regulations for HCFC/HFC refrigerant management in refrigeration plant.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: WorkSafeBC employer registration and occupational health and safety clearance (mandatory workers' compensation coverage); BC Fire Code compliance certificate and annual fire safety inspection; municipal structural occupancy and building permits; municipal plumbing and refrigeration inspections; and CFIA prerequisite sanitation and HACCP approval for raw meat handling areas.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA); online services include CRA My Business Account and Business Registration Online. British Columbia provincial tax administration is handled by the Ministry of Finance through its online services.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign corporation carrying on business in Canada generally obtains a CRA Business Number (BN) and the required program accounts, including an RT GST/HST account where registration is required or elected, through CRA Business Registration Online or by the applicable CRA registration process. The applicant must provide its legal name, jurisdiction and date of incorporation, registered and business addresses, business activities, ownership and authorized representative details, and relevant commencement and turnover information. A foreign entity may need to register extra-provincially in British Columbia before or while carrying on business there; provincial corporate registration does not replace CRA tax registration. A British Columbia ULC is a Canadian corporation and generally uses its BN for federal tax accounts. Non-resident applicants may need to use CRA procedures for non-residents where online registration is unavailable or inapplicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A British Columbia ULC is generally treated as a corporation for Canadian income-tax purposes and is subject to Canadian corporate tax; it is not a Canadian pass-through entity. Canada has no general domestic check-the-box election. If eligible under United States tax classification rules, a Canadian ULC may elect disregarded-entity or partnership treatment for US federal tax purposes by filing the applicable US election, commonly Form 8832. That foreign classification does not change Canadian classification and may create cross-border hybrid or treaty issues. Canadian hybrid-mismatch rules and treaty limitations may affect deductions, credits, or benefits; eligibility and consequences require transaction-specific review.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST), or Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) in participating provinces, plus British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST) on applicable transactions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in worldwide taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) for the small-supplier test, subject to statutory aggregation, timing, and other rules. The threshold is not a general exemption for every non-resident: non-resident persons carrying on business in Canada may be required to register without relying on the small-supplier threshold. British Columbia PST has separate registration rules and no equivalent general CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold applicable to all sellers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not generally require real-time tax-authority clearance, government digital stamping, or a universal API-based e-invoicing system for ordinary commercial supplies. GST/HST registrants must issue invoices or other supporting records containing prescribed information when required and retain records in an accessible form. Electronic records and invoices are permitted subject to CRA recordkeeping requirements. British Columbia PST documentation and collection obligations apply separately.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Qualifying goods supplied for export may be zero-rated under the Excise Tax Act where the statutory conditions are met, including applicable restrictions on delivery, possession, use, and export by the recipient. The supplier must retain evidence that the goods were exported and satisfy the relevant export rules; merely billing a non-resident or stating that goods are for export is insufficient. Services supplied to non-residents may be zero-rated only where the specific statutory conditions are met; exclusions apply, including certain services relating to Canadian real property, tangible personal property, or specified Canadian activities. Zero-rated supplies remain taxable supplies for registration and input-tax-credit purposes. British Columbia PST treatment is separate and must be assessed under provincial export and delivery rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian customs export declaration or other applicable export reporting record, where required
Bill of lading, air waybill, courier record, or other carrier evidence identifying the exported goods and destination
Commercial invoice, purchase order, and proof of payment or other transaction records
Proof of delivery or receipt outside Canada and records linking the goods to the export transaction
Inward remittance certificate is not a generally prescribed Canadian export zero-rating document; retain banking or payment evidence where relevant
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada imposes no general statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export proceeds. A supplier claiming zero-rating must retain adequate supporting records and substantiate eligibility on audit. An unsupported or incorrect zero-rating claim may result in assessment of GST/HST, interest, and applicable penalties, including gross-negligence penalties where statutory conditions are met; input tax credits or refunds may be denied or reassessed. False statements, evasion, or destruction or failure to retain required records may trigger additional civil or criminal consequences under applicable law.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) and OSFI for bank supervision; no separate foreign exchange administration authority in Canada
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada imposes no foreign exchange controls; the Canadian dollar is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. Profit remittances and capital repatriation by a BC ULC are unrestricted, subject only to anti-money laundering and tax-reporting obligations. Dividend or distribution payments require no central bank approval, but are reportable to the CRA and FINTRAC transaction reporting thresholds apply.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion of export proceeds exists. Export receipts in foreign currency may be retained in foreign-denominated accounts, converted freely at market rates, or used directly for import settlements without Bank of Canada authorization. FINTRAC reports are required for cross-border wire transfers of CAD 10,000 or more in one 24-hour period, and for large cash transactions.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium with legal restrictions. Canada does not recognise the EU EMI licence; non-resident payment service providers are regulated under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) and must register with EDD (Bank of Canada regional supervisor). FINTRAC registration as an MSB and any local licensing requirements apply to the BC ULC if it processes payments. Using an unregulated offshore EMI is not viable; only reputable fintech payment firms with Canadian MSB registration and BC corporate banking backstreets are acceptable.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors are not statutorily required to appear physically in BC for corporate account opening provided the financial institution completes Canada's mandated Client Identification and Verification (CIP) procedures. Remote video verification is generally permitted for low-risk operating accounts, subject to digital KYC acceptance and confirmation of the ULC's registration with BC Corporate Registry. In practice, tier-1 banks may require a notarised corporate resolution, director identification, and a video interview for the initial ULC relationship manager, especially for cross-border wires.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlimited liability structure flagged by compliance as a high-risk or unusual corporate personality
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the BC Certificate of Incorporation, Notice of Articles, company register extract, a reasoned corporate counsel memorandum explaining the ULC's pass-through eligibility and liability structure, plus audited or reviewed financial statements demonstrating the entity's operational substance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner and ultimate parent opacity due to non-resident shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a current beneficial-ownership register acceptable to FINTRAC and the bank, with passport/corporate extract of every direct or indirect beneficial holder above 25%, including a chain-of-title ownership diagram and evidence of each shareholder's identity and source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Freeze-dried pet food operations misclassified as an agriculture / animal-product money-laundering vulnerability
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide ISIC 1080 classification documentation, BC milk/inspection permits or CFIA registration, the health and export facility licence, plant inspection certificates, supplier invoices, and production bills of lading showing legitimate manufacturing activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border inbound capital injection with insufficient source-of-funds evidence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present the executed shareholder loan or share-subscription agreement, bank statements from the remitting bank, corporate valuations, tax-filing history showing no unreported income, and, if applicable, a foreign-exchange / pin translation statement for the injected funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-frequency settlement flows to off-exchange e-commerce platforms or unrelated raw-meat suppliers
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Build a treasury file containing proforma contracts, commercial invoices, packing lists, end-customer orders, customs import/export declarations, and a geo-spread vendor-mapping showing legitimate procurement from approved cold-chain suppliers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade settlement to high-risk or sanctioned counterparty namesakes
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Run continuous sanctions screening and produce a closed-loop compliance dossier showing the exact OFAC/OSFI/UN sanctions-screen result for each counterparty; include legal-entity identifiers (LEI) and beneficial ownership registry extracts for each supplier and buyer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 for direct credit from the foreign parent's or shareholder's custody bank to the BC ULC's operational account. The remitter must state a clean, factual purpose code such as 'Capital contribution' or 'Shareholder loan' in the payment narrative; no Bank of Canada approval is needed. Supporting documents include the subscription agreement, board/beneficial-owner resolution, and source-of-funds proof. For transfers above CAD 10,000, the receiving bank is obliged to record FINTRAC report and may request a formal capital-contribution closing package. Intercompany loans must be documented with an arm's-length interest rate and Canadian withholding-tax analysis; inbound equity is generally free of Canadian tax reporting beyond the CRA T106 for foreign-owned corporations.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 for direct suppliers, freight forwarders and royalty/licence settlements. For larger or documented raw-material purchases, an irrevocable, confirmed commercial letter of credit may be opened at the BC relationship bank under ICC UCP600 rules; payment is made by MT103 or MT202 against presentation of a complying shipping document set (commercial invoice, bill of lading, packing list, certificate of origin, and health certificate). For domestic Canadian clearing, use EFT/ACH lines (CPA) for BC suppliers and retail payroll. Same-day wire settlement for critical disbursements uses the Lynx system for CAD real-time gross settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forward (NDF) in emerging-market fringe currencies only if no deliverable market exists; CAD/USD NDFs are not standard but OTC-permissible
Cross-currency swaps (basis swaps) between CAD and USD or CAD and EUR
FX swaps (swap of principal at maturity)
FX options / zero-premium collars through regulated Canadian bank counterparties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report (provincial corporate renewal filing for the BC ULC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Finance – BC Corporate Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after each annual incorporation anniversary date, per s. 280 of the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Standard filing fee is CAD $58 (approx. USD $43); late filing imposes an escalating late fee and, if no annual report is filed for 2 consecutive years, the Registrar may strike the ULC from the register (administrative dissolution) after statutory notice and publication, with restoration available within 10 years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal Part I tax and BC provincial corporate income tax under the CRA single-administered return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within 6 months after the fiscal year-end; the final tax balance is due 3 months after year-end for a foreign-owned non-CCPC (typical ULC) or 2 months for a Canadian-controlled private corporation; instalments apply to large corporations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% for each complete month late (maximum 12 months) under ITA s. 162(1); CRA prescribed daily compound interest; gross-negligence penalty of 50% of understated tax under ITA s. 163; directors may be personally liable for unremitted withholding taxes under ITA s. 227.1.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST return (5% federal GST on taxable sales of freeze-dried pet food products; BC is a GST-only province outside the HST system)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filers (taxable revenue not exceeding CAD $1.5 million) file within 3 months after fiscal year-end; quarterly filers within 1 month after each quarter-end; monthly filers within 1 month after each month-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 5% of the net GST owing plus 1% per complete month late (maximum 12 months) under Excise Tax Act s. 280; daily interest on unremitted amounts; CRA may impose a third-party demand and directors can be liable for unremitted GST/HST under ETA s. 323.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC PST return (7% Provincial Sales Tax on taxable retail sales to BC end-consumers of pet treats, kibble and related goods)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Ministry of Finance – Revenue Division (Consumer Taxation Branch)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing frequency is set in the PST registration certificate, normally monthly with the return due by the last day of the following month; the Director of Revenue may allow quarterly or annual returns for qualifying low-remittance registrants
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of the PST owing plus interest on arrears under the Provincial Sales Tax Act (BC); directors can be personally liable for unremitted PST; prolonged default triggers assessment, collection enforcement and asset seizure.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The BC Business Corporations Act imposes no revenue, asset or shareholder-size audit threshold for a private ULC. An auditor may be appointed by shareholders, but the audit requirement is waived where all shareholders adopt a unanimous resolution under s. 232(1) (the standard election for a closely held ULC). An independent audit becomes compulsory only if the waiver is not passed or if the ULC is a reporting issuer (not applicable to a private manufacturing ULC).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable enterprises; a private ULC applies Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE), or IFRS where the parent shareholder or lender requires it. CRA accepts either framework for the T2 return and financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under s. 398 of the BC Business Corporations Act, the ULC must keep a register of individuals with significant control (ISC register) at its statutory records office. The register is not filed with the Registrar; however, every share transfer or change of significant control must be entered within 15 days of the event. The annual corporate secretarial review must re-confirm the continuing accuracy of the ISC register, directors, registered office and minute book, because a knowingly false or stale register is an offence subject to fines, and the register must be available for authorized inspection.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD $225 – $1,200 per year (CAD $300 – $1,600) for a BC registered records office and corporate agent; higher if outsourced corporate secretarial administration is included
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD $6,000 – $19,000 (CAD $8,000 – $25,000) for a certified independent audit of a small private ULC manufacturing entity, where shareholders do not waive the audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% (15% federal general rate + 12% British Columbia general corporate rate)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Federal Manufacturing and Processing profits deduction reduces qualifying freeze-dried manufacturing income to 13.5% federal, giving a combined 25.5% rate; qualified Canadian-controlled private corporation CCPC active business income benefits from 9% federal and 2% BC small business rates on the first CAD 500,000; SR&ED investment tax credit of 15%; accelerated capital cost allowance for clean-energy generation and qualifying manufacturing equipment.
